01: Respecting the elderly is a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation. It is deeply rooted in the thoughts and behaviour of the Chinese people and is a code of conduct and a social norm that people generally observe. In China today this virtue is widely passed on. All sectors of society are actively creating a social atmosphere in which the elderly are respected and helped. Providing convenient services for older people has become a social consensus: communities, for example, have set up canteens especially for senior citizens, and priority seats are provided in public places. The government has also introduced a series of policies that give strong protection to the rights and interests of the elderly. Respecting the elderly is an important cornerstone of social harmony and development, for it helps foster a sound social atmosphere and drives the progress of civilization across society.
02:
The Chinese nation values the spirit of self-reliance and self-improvement. This spirit is deeply embedded in Chinese culture and is an important support for the survival and development of the nation.

Since the start of reform and opening up, China has, on its journey of self-reliance, continued to increase investment in scientific research and has kept making new breakthroughs in such fields as information technology, artificial intelligence and space engineering. 5G networks now cover the whole country, telemedicine is developing rapidly, the use of electronic payment leads the world, and the Chang'e lunar exploration programme has demonstrated eye-catching progress in space. The spirit of self-reliance has become a powerful driving force behind the country's modernization and inspires the Chinese people to keep pressing ahead for the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation.
03: Frugality is a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation. In ancient China productivity was low, and our ancestors knew well that the fruits of labour were hard-won, so they held to the idea of frugality. Today, when material goods are extremely abundant, the Chinese people still keep to a frugal way of life, which reflects a philosophy of rational consumption and a respect for labour. In recent years the Chinese government has continued to strengthen the building of a conservation-minded society, promoting the "Clean Plate Campaign", reducing food waste, encouraging a simple and low-carbon lifestyle, advancing resource recycling and opposing excessive consumption. The building of a conservation-minded society has strongly driven the high-quality development of China's economy.
04: The Tiangong Space Station is China's first space laboratory. It has more than 110 cubic metres of usable space, can accommodate three astronauts, and orbits 400 to 450 kilometres above the Earth's surface. More than 180 scientific research and application projects have been carried out on the station, covering such fields as space life science, space medicine and space materials science. The research results obtained there have been widely applied in China and have produced remarkable economic benefits. Space breeding, for example, has generated direct economic benefits of up to hundreds of billions of yuan. This not only marks the tremendous progress China has made in space technology, but also shows that China has made a major contribution to global space research and application.
05: Boasting a favourable geographical location, the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area has well-developed transport infrastructure and rich industrial resources. It is one of the most open and economically dynamic regions in China and holds an important strategic position in the country's economic development. The Greater Bay Area will be built not only into a vibrant world-class city cluster and an international centre of scientific and technological innovation with global influence, but also into a high-quality living circle suitable for working, shopping and travelling. As reform and opening up deepen, the development of the Greater Bay Area will further boost the regional economy. By 2035 it will have become a first-class bay area in the world.
06: Since ancient times China's water resources have been scarce in the north and abundant in the south, with an extremely uneven distribution. To effectively solve the serious water shortage in the north, the Chinese government has carried out the South-to-North Water Diversion Project. It is a huge water conservancy project that allocates water resources across regions. After decades of planning and preparation, construction began in 2002. The project consists of three routes—east, middle and west—with a total length of 4,350 kilometres, and will benefit more than 400 million people. Since water began flowing in 2014, more than 50 billion cubic metres have been diverted to the north, providing reliable water resources for the people there, greatly improving the ecological environment of the region and promoting sustainable and sound economic development.
07: The successful development of the Beidou Navigation Satellite System is a major scientific and technological achievement China has made since reform and opening up. Through unremitting efforts, researchers overcame a series of technical difficulties, and the Beidou system finally achieved global coverage and high-precision positioning, making China one of the few countries in the world that independently own a global satellite navigation system. Beidou is now widely used in many fields, including transport, disaster relief, weather forecasting and public security. It has won wide international recognition and is beginning to provide quality services to more and more countries and regions.
08: Yangshan Port is an important part of the Shanghai shipping centre. It is China's first deep-water port and one of the largest deep-water ports in the world. After nearly 20 years of development the port has become highly automated. The use of digital technology and artificial intelligence has greatly reduced labour costs and carbon emissions. The self-developed terminal management system can control large equipment remotely from a hundred kilometres away. Yangshan Port looks busy, yet no manual operation is visible on site, and it can run around the clock. The port will keep growing and make greater contributions to building Shanghai into a global shipping centre.
09: Travelling in space has always been a dream of the Chinese nation. In 2003 the Shenzhou-5 spacecraft was launched successfully, and Yang Liwei became the first Chinese astronaut to fly into space. In 2008 Shenzhou-7 lifted off, and Zhai Zhigang became the first astronaut in Chinese history to perform a spacewalk. In recent years China's space programme has entered a fast lane of innovation and development, space infrastructure has been steadily advanced, and the Chinese space station was completed in 2022. The rapid development of China's space endeavour has written a glorious page in the history of the Chinese nation and made a great contribution to the progress of human civilization. In the future China will take steadier and farther steps in exploring space.
10: Traditional Chinese wedding customs have a long history. A complete set of wedding ceremonies gradually took shape as early as the Zhou Dynasty, and some of them are still in use today. Chinese wedding customs have changed a great deal, yet wedding ceremonies are still very grand. The venue is carefully decorated, with red—the colour symbolizing jubilance—as the main tone, and is filled with objects that wish the couple happiness. At the wedding the couple bow to Heaven and Earth, to their parents and to each other; then they host a banquet for the guests and propose a toast to thank them. Today many young people are still fond of traditional Chinese weddings and enjoy a unique and beautiful Chinese-style romance.
11: China abounds in bamboo and was the first country to develop and use bamboo resources. Bamboo grows widely across the country in a great many varieties. It is highly practical and is used in many areas of production and daily life, such as making chopsticks, tables and chairs, and building bridges and houses. The Chinese love bamboo. Since ancient times countless men of letters have taken bamboo as their theme and created a wealth of brilliant literary and painterly works. The straight stem of bamboo symbolizes integrity of character. Bamboo has great vitality and adaptability: however harsh the environment, it can survive tenaciously, and it therefore stands for an unyielding spirit. For thousands of years bamboo has been regarded as a symbol of the character of the Chinese nation.
12: Fans have been popular with the Chinese since ancient times, but today they are no longer merely a tool for cooling off; they are appreciated more as works of art. Many fans are gracefully shaped and finely made, and are painted with exquisite designs of landscapes, flowers and birds, or figures, which gives them high artistic value. Many well-known Chinese painters and calligraphers like to write poems and paint on fans to show their artistic taste. Fans are often given as gifts to express good wishes and sincere feelings. Today the practical function of fans has greatly diminished, but as a cultural symbol and an art form they still play an important role in traditional Chinese culture.
13: In China, as an ageing society approaches, care for the elderly has drawn widespread attention. What people talk about most is what model of elderly care should be adopted. Most believe that the model should be diversified. Government guidance and social participation can be used to set up more and better elderly care institutions, improve community service centres and encourage self-care at home; a model combining family care with social care can also be promoted. As the government and society keep increasing their input into elderly care services, facilities will be upgraded, service quality will improve step by step, and older people will live more conveniently, comfortably, healthily and happily.
14: With economic and social development, China's population structure has changed markedly and the country has gradually entered an ageing society. The elderly population will keep growing and the trend of population ageing will become more pronounced. To meet the various challenges brought by population ageing, the state is actively taking measures and increasing support for elderly care. By reforming the social security system, the government keeps increasing social security funding and gradually expanding coverage so that more older people benefit. The government also encourages all kinds of social organizations to provide services for the elderly. With the joint efforts of the government and social organizations, older people will live happier lives.
15: In recent years China's elderly population has kept growing. The Chinese government is taking various measures to advance the building of an elderly care service system so that older people can live healthily and happily in their later years. Elderly care institutions of various kinds have been built across the country. To improve the quality of their services, the government has issued a series of standards and strengthened supervision over such institutions. To make dining easier for older people, many cities have opened community canteens that offer affordable meals. Those with limited mobility can also enjoy door-to-door meal delivery. At the same time China is actively exploring other models such as home-based and community-based care to ensure that all older people are provided for.
16: In recent years more and more Chinese cultural products have entered the global market and are increasingly favoured by overseas consumers. With the rapid growth of China's cultural trade with other countries, the export value of Chinese cultural products has ranked among the world's highest for many years running, and a group of cultural enterprises, products and brands with international influence have emerged. Data show that overseas sales of Chinese publications, films and television works, online literature and animation have risen year after year. The Chinese government has introduced a series of policies to encourage and support more outstanding cultural products with Chinese elements to go abroad, expand their overseas market share and further enhance the worldwide influence of Chinese culture.
17: With the rapid development of China's economy and the steady improvement of people's living standards, urban residents are setting ever higher demands on their environment and quality of life. Local governments in China are paying more attention to building and improving public facilities so as to better meet people's needs. By building new squares, parks and public green spaces, or by redesigning and renovating existing public sites, many cities have provided residents with more places for leisure and socializing. Today fitness equipment bought with government funds and fitness trails laid by the government can be seen everywhere in many cities, which has noticeably improved conditions for outdoor activities and made the cities more beautiful.
18: In recent years Chinese cities have developed faster and the urban living environment has improved markedly. Many cities have worked hard to explore a path of high-quality urban development with Chinese characteristics, and urban functions have been steadily improved and governance noticeably enhanced. China has continued to carry out ecological restoration and functional repair in cities, comprehensively renovated old urban residential areas, vigorously promoted urban landscaping and greening, and eliminated pollution. At the same time it has vigorously advanced the systematic construction of urban infrastructure, carried out surveys of buildings and municipal facilities, and investigated and rectified potential safety hazards, in an effort to create a high-quality living environment and make cities more beautiful, safer and more liveable.
19:
Zhang Qian was the first great explorer in China. Braving hardships and overcoming one difficulty after another, he was sent to the Western Regions twice, opened up trade between China and West Asia and Europe, carried Chinese silk and silk fabrics to West Asia and Europe, and pioneered the famous Silk Road in history. At the same time he introduced the local customs, geography and culture and the unique species of the Western Regions to the Central Plains, which greatly broadened people's horizons.

As historians have pointed out, without Zhang Qian's missions to the Western Regions the Silk Road could not have been opened, nor would there have been cultural exchanges between the Han Dynasty and the Western Regions or Europe.
